whatFailed: Step 2 asserted that a REST GET for a nonexistent documentId answers error.message "Entity not found", the documented constructor default of the @strapi/utils NotFoundError class, but the public REST 404 is produced by the ctx.notFound() fallback in the errors middleware and carries node's reason phrase "Not Found" instead.

docClaim.quote: The `NotFoundError` class is a generic error class for throwing `404` status code errors. It accepts the following parameters: | `message` | `string` | The error message | `Entity not found` |

observed: GET /api/articles/guardmissingdocument0000 answered 404 with {"data":null,"error":{"status":404,"name":"NotFoundError","message":"Not Found","details":{}}}. Step 1, which asserted the envelope shape (data null, status 404, name NotFoundError, non-empty message, details present), passed on the same body. Only the exact message wording failed. The body is byte-for-byte what formatHttpError(createError(404, 'Not Found', { details: {} })) produces, which proves the http-errors path, not the @strapi/utils class path, served it.
impact: None from the assertion as written: the bound doc claim is about the class constructor default and the product honors it exactly. The run does however incidentally surface a real, separate documentation bug in docs.strapi.io/cms/api/rest (see notes), which the scenario failed to encode.

rootCause.explanation: This explains the observed wire message; it is not a product defect against the bound claim. The core-api collection-type service findOne (packages/core/core/src/core-api/service/collection-type.ts:55-62) delegates to strapi.documents(uid).findOne, which returns null for a missing documentId. The controller findOne (packages/core/core/src/core-api/controller/collection-type.ts:36-45) passes that null to transformResponse, which short-circuits on isNil and returns null (packages/core/core/src/core-api/controller/transform.ts:47-49). returnBodyMiddleware then skips assigning ctx.body because the value is nil (packages/core/core/src/services/server/compose-endpoint.ts:64-70), so ctx.response._explicitStatus stays false and the errors middleware falls through to ctx.notFound() at line 18. That helper is generated in packages/core/core/src/services/server/koa.ts:12-21 with `response = statusName`, where statusName is node's STATUS_CODES[404] = 'Not Found'; it builds an http-errors instance (whose own class name happens to also be 'NotFoundError') and renders it through formatHttpError (packages/core/core/src/services/errors.ts:49-62). The @strapi/utils NotFoundError class with its 'Entity not found' default (packages/core/utils/src/errors.ts:70-77) is never constructed on this path, so the doc's documented default cannot appear here. Verified by reading each file, not inferred from names.

introducedBy.title: refactor error handling
introducedBy.note: Names the origin of the observed 'Not Found' wording, not a defect. This commit (Pierre Noel, no PR number in the message) added both the `if (!ctx.response._explicitStatus) return ctx.notFound()` fallback and the generated koa error helpers whose default argument is node's reason phrase. The wording has been stable ever since: the 2026-06-25 refactor 6f6af340081 'feat(ts): augment all context error response methods (#25424)' swapped the `statuses` package for node:http STATUS_CODES but statuses(404) and STATUS_CODES[404] are both 'Not Found', so behavior is unchanged. The class default 'Entity not found' at packages/core/utils/src/errors.ts:75 traces to 728d614ca41 (Marc Roig, 2023-11-16, the TS conversion) over the same 2021 class. Conclusion: no regression, the assertion was never true of this endpoint in any Strapi 5 build.

notes:
Two things worth separating.

1. The failing assertion is mis-bound. error-handling.md documents 'Entity not found' as the default argument of the NotFoundError constructor, under the 'Throwing errors' half of the page, that is, what a developer gets when their own code runs `throw new errors.NotFoundError()` with no message. It is not a promise about what any built-in endpoint returns. The product honors that default exactly (packages/core/utils/src/errors.ts:75), so there is no violation of the bound claim. The scenario's own step note concedes the step is 'Expected RED, and deliberately so', which is the tell: it encoded a wording no bound doc promises for this request. The generator was almost certainly misled by the response's `"name": "NotFoundError"`, which is a genuine coincidence, http-errors names its 404 class NotFoundError too, so the envelope looks like the @strapi/utils class produced it when it did not.

2. There IS a real documentation bug next door, and the scenario pointed at it without asserting it. docs.strapi.io/cms/api/rest documents the 404 for GET /api/:pluralApiId/:documentId as {"data": null, "error": {"status": 404, "name": "NotFoundError", "message": "Document not found"}} (snapshot .truecourse/specs/sources/docs.strapi.io/cms/api/rest.md:214-221). The product answers 'Not Found' for that exact request and has since 2021. That doc text lives in the separate strapi/documentation repo, not in the tested checkout. A correctly encoded scenario for this endpoint should expect 'Not Found' and bind rest.md, and the finding to file is a docs fix in strapi/documentation.

3. For the doc author: the product genuinely carries three different 404 wordings, which is what the scenario author was reaching for. Public REST core-api answers 'Not Found' (the ctx.notFound() fallback). The content-manager admin API and the MCP handlers throw errors.NotFoundError('Document not found') and 'Document not found.' (packages/core/content-manager/server/src/mcp/handlers/constants.ts:1-3, packages/core/content-manager/server/src/controllers/collection-types.ts:696, packages/core/content-manager/server/src/preview/controllers/validation/preview.ts:43). The bare class default is 'Entity not found'. rest.md appears to have copied the admin-panel wording onto the public REST endpoint. Note also that the observed 404 carries `details: {}` and rest.md's sample omits `details` entirely, a second small drift on the same sample.

4. One structural note on the endpoint itself, offered as an observation rather than a finding: the public REST 404 for a missing document is not raised deliberately by the controller. It is the generic 'no handler set a body' fallback in the errors middleware. That is why the message is a bare HTTP reason phrase and why `details` is empty. If Strapi ever wants the REST 404 to say 'Document not found' as its docs claim, the fix is for the core-api findOne controller to throw errors.NotFoundError('Document not found') on a nil entity rather than relying on the fallback.
